findings.quote: management sizes the AI-accelerator market at more than $1.4 trillion by 2030 and the server-CPU market above $220 billion
findings.issue: The transcript sizes both markets as "approximately $1.4 trillion by 2030" and "approximately $220 billion by 2030"; the "more than" in the source attaches to the growth rate ("grow more than 45% annually", "more than 50% annually"), not the endpoint. The report reassigns "more than"/"above" to the TAM figures, turning management's central estimate into a floor and overstating a number that carries the growth/TAM argument.
findings.fix: Match the source: write "approximately $1.4 trillion by 2030" and "approximately $220 billion," or move the "more than" onto the growth rates (">45% annually", ">50% annually") exactly as the transcript states them.
findings.note: Reconfirmed on re-check: points[3] still reads "grow more than 45% a year to about $1.4 trillion by 2030 and the server-CPU market more than 50% a year to about $220 billion," matching the transcript. Unchanged by the latest trim.

findings.quote: the company can self-fund its roadmap and its acquisitions ... the company can fund its roadmap and acquisitions from its own resources without leaning on debt
findings.issue: The self-funding conclusion is stated twice in the two-paragraph field in near-identical words: paragraph one ends "leverage is not a constraint and the company can self-fund its roadmap and its acquisitions," and paragraph two ends "the company can fund its roadmap and acquisitions from its own resources without leaning on debt." The same claim made twice adds nothing and wastes the field's room.
findings.fix: State the self-funding point once. Close the second paragraph on a distinct thought (e.g. the tangible-book caveat, or interest coverage) rather than repeating that AMD can fund its roadmap and acquisitions.
findings.note: Reconfirmed on re-check: balanceCommentary is unchanged by the latest trim. Paragraph one still ends "so leverage is not a constraint"; the self-funding point is stated once, in paragraph two.

findings.quote: There is a single class of common stock, so public shareholders hold both the economics and the vote, without the super-voting structure common among newer technology issuers.
findings.issue: The proxy excerpt supports a single common-stock class only indirectly (the ownership table denominates everything in one "common stock" with a single "Percent of Class" on 1,630,338,779 shares). It says nothing about voting structure, super-voting shares, or peer issuers. The clause "without the super-voting structure common among newer technology issuers" is an editorial comparison the excerpt does not carry, and the prompt requires governance claims to rest on the proxy excerpt.
findings.fix: Keep the claim to what the ownership table shows (a single class of common stock, proportional voting). Drop the unsupported "super-voting structure common among newer technology issuers" generalization, or ground it.
findings.note: Reconfirmed on re-check: governance is unchanged by the latest trim. The clause still reads only "There is a single class of common stock, so public shareholders hold both the economics and the vote."

findings.quote: grew revenue 23% year-over-year in the quarter on record mobile and commercial demand
findings.issue: The transcript supports a record only for mobile ("record mobile processor revenue") and for client processor revenue overall; it does not describe "record" commercial demand — commercial is characterized as Ryzen PRO sales "growing more than 50% year-over-year" and adoption that "continued to expand." Attaching "record" to commercial as well as mobile extends the superlative past what the source shows.
findings.fix: Confine "record" to what the transcript states — "record mobile processor revenue" — and describe commercial as growing/expanding (Ryzen PRO +50% YoY) rather than record.
findings.note: Reconfirmed on re-check: segments[1].body is unchanged by the latest trim, still reading "strong mobile and commercial demand," not "record."

findings.quote: a stock priced near its high on a rich multiple
findings.issue: The valuation motif is repeated near-verbatim across the report: the subtitle ("priced richly near its 52-week high"), analystCommentary ("a stock priced near its high on a rich multiple"), thesis ("trades near its high on a trailing multiple"), valuation ("a stock that has run hard and sits near its high") and finalRecommendation ("near the high on a rich multiple"). The probability-weighted fair value "$565.00 ... about 12% above the price" likewise recurs verbatim in analystCommentary, scenarioCommentary and finalRecommendation. It is the report's central point, but the same phrasing repeated five-plus times is a tic past the point of notice.
findings.fix: Introduce the "near its high on a rich multiple" point and the $565 / ~12% fair value once each, then refer back in varied words. Let each section add its own angle rather than restate the same phrase.
findings.note: Reduced but still open: the "high on a rich multiple" family fell from 5x to 3x (analystCommentary, thesis.body, risks[0]); finalRecommendation now varies away ("after a steep run", "climbed steeply over the past year"). But two of the three survivors still carry the identical six-word clause verbatim rather than a paraphrase: thesis.body ("near its high on a rich multiple, offers a risk/reward that no longer favors the buyer") and risks[0] ("priced near its high on a rich multiple"). "$565.00 ... about 12% above the price" still repeats verbatim in analystCommentary and scenarioCommentary.

findings.quote: the asset base is heavy with goodwill and intangibles from the Xilinx and ZT Systems deals, so reported book value overstates tangible capital
findings.issue: The grounding surface carries no goodwill, intangibles or tangible-book-value figure — only total equity ($63.0B FY25). The claim that the asset base is "heavy with goodwill and intangibles" and that book value "overstates tangible capital" is a quantitative characterization the pack does not support, even if the FY21-to-FY22 equity step-up hints at it.
findings.fix: Either ground the point in a figure the pack carries, or soften it to what is on the surface (e.g. the large equity step-up coinciding with the Xilinx stock deal) rather than asserting the goodwill/intangibles weighting and tangible-capital overstatement outright.
findings.note: Reconfirmed on re-check: the goodwill/intangibles/tangible-capital sentence remains absent from balanceCommentary, unchanged by the latest trim.

findings.issue: The BUY-to-HOLD rewrite introduced two new phrasings that now recur verbatim across sections, a fresh instance of the same tic F-5 flags. "balanced rather than favorable" appears 3x — analystCommentary ("the risk/reward from here is balanced rather than favorable"), thesis ("offers a balanced rather than favorable risk/reward") and finalRecommendation.body[1] ("the payoff is balanced rather than favorable"). "below the Street" also appears 3x — analystCommentary ("target range $420-$720, below the Street"), valuation.multiplesCommentary ("a target below the Street and a wide range") and finalRecommendation.body[1] ("We stop at HOLD, below the Street's target"). The same HOLD-positioning claim is restated in near-identical words in three places rather than made once and pointed to.
findings.fix: State the "balanced rather than favorable" payoff judgment and the "below the Street" positioning once each (analystCommentary is the natural home), then refer back in varied words from thesis, valuation and finalRecommendation. Let each section add its own angle rather than repeat the stock phrase.
findings.note: Addressed: "balanced rather than favorable" now appears once (analystCommentary only, down from 3x); "below the Street" fell from 3x to 2x (analystCommentary, valuation.multiplesCommentary). finalRecommendation.body[1], the closest near-identical duplicate ("We stop at HOLD, below the Street's target"), now reads "short of the Street's target," a genuine reword. The two remaining "below the Street" uses sit in directly related sections (the HOLD call and the valuation basis for it), not the three-way near-identical restatement the finding named.
